status: Mixed by theme. Closed on 30 Jul 2026: energy and climate innovations, gasification of residual streams, hydrogen and green chemistry, Biobased Circular (small). applicants: Individual companies acting at their own cost and risk, or participants in a partnership with at least one company; provinces and municipalities may join but cannot receive subsidy; water boards can in some cases. Applies in NL including Bonaire, St Eustatius and Saba.
funding_rate: Maximum rates (Handleiding 2026): pilots 25% for companies (80% for research bodies' non-economic activity); test infrastructure 25%; demonstrations: environmental or other CO2 measures 40% of extra investment cost (30% for CCS/CCU; halved if no reference scenario); energy efficiency 30% of extra cost; energy efficiency in buildings 25% of total cost; renewable energy and renewable hydrogen 45% (30% for storage or specific hydrogen infrastructure); circular economy 40% of extra cost; infrastructure 30% (art. 46) or 50% (art. 56); gasification 40-45% by category. Uplift for all project types: +10 points medium and +20 points small firms.
caps: Demonstration up to EUR 30M; pilot and test infrastructure up to EUR 25M; built environment EUR 1M; Biobased Circular pilot EUR 1M and demonstration EUR 10M (large-project sub-theme above those amounts up to EUR 25M and 30M); gasification EUR 30M; built-environment de minimis support EUR 300,000 per company over 36 months
budget: Regular themes EUR 134M; built environment EUR 6M; circular economy and Biobased Circular large EUR 60M; Biobased Circular EUR 22M; hydrogen and green chemistry EUR 38M; gasification EUR 150M
stacking: Other national subsidies reduce DEI+ support; SDE++, Horizon, provincial and municipal subsidies are not deducted in advance
eligible_costs: Pilots: wages plus 50% overhead, or fixed EUR 80 per hour (raised from EUR 60 in 2026), or full-cost method, plus depreciation of equipment, materials and third-party costs. window: Themes have separate windows; circular economy and large biobased: 16 Jun to 17 Dec 2026
before_start: Yes: no start, order or commitment before the application is filed; start within 6 months of the grant; project max 4 years; CO2 reduction in NL within 10 years of the start
assessment: First come, first served by date of complete application; 8 weeks, extendable by 8; positive decisions sent by mid-December because the budget is for 2026 only

name: DHI (Demonstratieprojecten, Haalbaarheidsstudies, Investeringsvoorbereidingsprojecten)
summary: Demonstration, feasibility and investment-preparation projects in foreign markets.
ignite_tags: sector: All sectors | size: ≤250 employees | scope: National | topic: International | type: Grant
legal_basis: DHI regulation, Staatscourant 2026, nr. 7891
status: OPEN 2 Mar to 31 Dec 2026, or until the budget is used; assessed in order of arrival (RVO pages checked 30 Oct 2026)
applicants: SMEs with legal personality (not sole traders, VOF, CV or maatschap) in NL or the Caribbean part of the Kingdom, registered at KVK; collaborations may include a large company. Needs at least 3 employees in NL, EUR 100,000 turnover over the last 3 years, no other DHI project running, and de minimis headroom (EUR 300,000 over 3 years).
size_rule: SME with legal personality; at least 3 employees in NL (structural hiring counts); EUR 100,000 turnover over 3 years
funding_rate: 50% of project costs, or 70% for green projects (climate or circular economy; RVO screening framework), for demonstration, feasibility and investment-preparation projects. Minimum subsidy EUR 25,000 (costs of at least EUR 50,000).
caps: Demonstration up to EUR 200,000 (max 3 years); feasibility up to EUR 100,000 (max 2 years); investment preparation up to EUR 100,000, and in 2026 time costs in NL and abroad together max EUR 75,000; market validation (new in 2026) EUR 25,000 for start-ups up to ten years old when costs are at least EUR 50,000, max 40 in 2026 (20 in developing countries, 20 elsewhere)
budget: EUR 8.5M for 2026 (RVO news, 2 Mar 2026)
instrument_detail: Four parts: demonstration, feasibility study, investment preparation, market validation. Technology must be TRL 8 or 9 for demonstration and feasibility. Export of at least 10 times the subsidy (5 times in developing countries) within 3 years of a demonstration; investment of at least 5 times the subsidy within 3 years of an investment-preparation project.
stacking: De minimis ceiling EUR 300,000 over three years
eligible_costs: Demonstration: hardware by depreciation, transport and related costs; time spent in NL may not exceed time spent abroad. Feasibility: study costs and a report for the foreign customer; no market research. Investment preparation: study, small trial production, outside expertise up to 50% of costs.
excluded_costs: Developing new technology or adapting the product for the foreign market; sales activities such as quotations and promotional material; selling the demonstration hardware to the host
channel: RVO e-Loket with eHerkenning level 2+ (RVO login for the Caribbean); quick scan available by email before applying
window: 2 Mar 2026 to 31 Dec 2026, or until the budget is used (first come, first served)
before_start: RVO says that once an application is approved, work can start; the exact start-date rule sits in the regulation text (Staatscourant 2026, 7891) and was not read
assessment: Order of arrival; 90% advance on approval; yearly progress report for projects over 1 year; payout request within 13 weeks of completion; decision on it within 13 weeks; management statement needed for subsidies of EUR 125,000 or more
per_period_limit: Only one running DHI project at a time
fit_signals: Dutch SME proving technology to foreign buyers or preparing a foreign investment
confidence: High: rates, caps, eligibility, window, budget and post-award rules from RVO's four DHI pages and the process page
conflicts: RESOLVED: the earlier consultancy rate gap is closed; RVO states 50% or 70%. Earlier note that time costs in investment preparation are capped at EUR 75,000 is confirmed.
open_questions: Read Staatscourant 7891 for the exact start-date rule
